### Hermogenes David Rios

I am Hermogenes David Rios, a senior studying Economics and Statistics at [Macalester College](https://www.macalester.edu) in Saint Paul, Minnesota (graduating in May 2027). I work in applied econometrics and causal inference, using data to separate what a policy or an event actually caused from what was already underway. Learn more [about me](experience.qmd).


### Highlights

[**Research Assistant on Three Projects This Summer:**](experience.qmd#research) I estimate the health effects of a Twin Cities waste incinerator using causal inference methods in R, audit the analysis pipeline for a randomized controlled trial of a digital-literacy curriculum in Punjab, India, and recovered 17,000 households for a study of how mobile phone access shapes gender attitudes in Sub-Saharan Africa.

[**Author of "Immigration, Gender, and Citizenship":**](/posts/metrics/) Quantified labor market disparities using Mincer earnings regressions and a Blinder-Oaxaca decomposition on 500K+ census records. Published in the *Macalester Street Journal: Equilibrium*, Vol. 3 (2025).

[**Founder of *Camino a la U*:**](/posts/camino/) In January 2026, I received a \$2,000 Live It Fund grant from Macalester's [Entrepreneurship and Innovation Department](https://www.macalester.edu/entrepreneurship-and-innovation/turning-vision-into-action-live-it-fund-j-term-2026-projects/) to found *Camino a la U*, a university-access program for low-income students in Santa Cruz, Bolivia. I designed the selection process and organized five teachers to coach students through admission essays and entrance exams, raising average admission-exam scores by 52 percentage points (from 32% to 84%).


<h3 style="margin-bottom: 0.15rem;">Skills</h3>
<p style="margin-bottom: 0;">R, Stata, Python, SQL, Excel, LaTeX, Econometrics, Causal Inference, Machine Learning</p>
